purpose: Miglitol is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is used along with diet and exercise, and sometimes with other diabetes medicines. It helps keep your blood sugar from spiking too high after meals.
how_it_works: When you eat carbohydrates like bread, pasta, or rice, your body breaks them down into sugar. Miglitol slows down the enzymes in your intestines that do this job, so sugar enters your bloodstream more slowly and gradually. This helps prevent those sharp jumps in blood sugar that happen right after eating.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are stomach-related, including gas, bloating, diarrhea, and stomach pain. These are usually worse at the start of treatment and often improve as your body adjusts. Taking the medicine with food as directed can help reduce these effects.
warnings: Miglitol on its own does not cause low blood sugar, but if you take it with other diabetes medicines like insulin or sulfonylureas, your blood sugar could drop too low. If that happens, you must treat low blood sugar with regular glucose tablets or glucose gel, NOT table sugar or juice, because miglitol slows sugar absorption. Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease, bowel problems, or digestive disorders before taking this medicine.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 25 mg taken three times a day with the first bite of each main meal. Your doctor may gradually increase your dose to 50 mg or up to 100 mg three times daily depending on how well your blood sugar is controlled and how well you tolerate the medicine.
